description:
## What

In `src/fetcher/circuit_breaker.cr`, `recovery_timeout_elapsed?` uses `Time.utc - last_failure >= @recovery_timeout` to decide when an open circuit breaker should transition to half-open. `@last_failure_time` is written via `Time.utc` in `record_failure` and `allow_request?`. The same wall-clock-vs-monotonic problem we just fixed in the stress specs (commit e79213c).

## Why

NTP corrections or system suspend/resume can jump the wall clock. A backwards jump makes the recovery timeout appear elapsed prematurely, transitioning the breaker to half-open too early. A forwards jump keeps the circuit stuck open past the intended recovery time. `Time.monotonic` never goes backwards and is the right primitive for elapsed-time comparisons.

## How

```crystal
private def recovery_timeout_elapsed? : Bool
  if last_failure = @last_failure_time
    Time.monotonic - last_failure >= @recovery_timeout
  else
    false
  end
end
```

Update the two writes in `record_failure` and `allow_request?` to use `Time.monotonic`. Update field type to `Time?` (it's already that, just a value change).

## Note on scope

The same `Time.utc` elapsed-time pattern exists in ValidatedIpStore, RegistryHelpers, and BoundedRegistry. Those are a system-wide pattern fix (separate ticket / OpenSpec candidate). This ticket is the single-file, surgical fix for CircuitBreaker.

## Done when

- `Time.monotonic` used for `@last_failure_time` writes and `recovery_timeout_elapsed?` comparison
- `spec/circuit_breaker_spec.cr` still passes
- Full spec suite still green
title: Fix: use Time.monotonic in CircuitBreaker timeout logic
